study type: observational study comparing two consecutive cohorts
exposure: Concurrent oral misoprostol administration with cervical ripening balloon (CRB)
Sequential oral misoprostol administration with cervical ripening balloon (CRB)
cohort: Two consecutive cohorts of women with unfavorable cervix undergoing induction of labor by means of a double-balloon cervical ripening balloon combined with oral misoprostol.
finding: Concurrent administration of misoprostol with CRB significantly shortened the time to active labor and vaginal delivery compared to sequential administration, with a similar rate of vaginal delivery and no increase in adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Concurrent misoprostol with CRB resulted in a similar rate of vaginal delivery compared to the sequential scheme (63.9% vs. 76.7%, P=0.29).
